title: Data Centre Votes, GIFs and AI Coding Deals
points: OpenAI launched Images 2.6 with GIF creation and 50% faster image generation in ChatGPT, Codex and its API.
US midterm voters backed limits on data centers in nearly every local vote counted so far, putting AI buildout plans under pressure.
OpenAI is buying Pierre Computer and Meta bought Conductor, as both push deeper into AI coding tools.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Mei: US voters just backed limits on data centers in 38 of 39 fully counted local votes, according to trackers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So the cloud has a neighbour problem.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily, Friday 6 November 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things in 30 seconds. One: OpenAI launched Images 2.6, with GIF creation and 50% faster image generation in ChatGPT, Codex and its API.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Two: US midterm voters backed limits on data centers in nearly every local vote counted so far. That puts AI buildout plans under pressure.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three: OpenAI is buying Pierre Computer, and Meta bought Conductor. Both are pushing deeper into AI coding tools.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: First, the vote. Local measures restricting data centers won 38 of 39 fully counted votes, according to trackers. An NBC exit poll found 76% of voters would oppose one in their community.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Is that just a few loud neighbours?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Doesn't look like it. Goldman Sachs reportedly sees 45% of planned US capacity at risk of temporary freezes. And Texas's governor-elect campaigned on a halt.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Temporary freezes, so not cancelled for good?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: That is how it is reported. Think of a new hawker centre. Everyone loves the food, but nobody wants the exhaust fan outside their window.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And for a company like Shopee?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The computing power behind AI tools could get tighter or pricier. That is worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So the one thing to remember: AI needs buildings, and the neighbours get a vote.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Second, OpenAI launched Images 2.6. It runs about 50% faster, and it can turn a prompt or a photo into a looping GIF. It is in ChatGPT, Codex and its API.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Can you tweak the GIF, or is it take it or leave it?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: You can edit the speed and the frames. Users can also save reference pictures to keep characters consistent.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So the mascot looks the same on every poster, instead of getting a new face each time.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Exactly. Developers get two API models, which are ways to plug it into their own tools. Flare is for speed, and Sunburst is for detail.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And for people at Shopee?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Marketing teams could produce campaign visuals and short animated banners faster. That is worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember: faster images, GIFs, and a mascot that stays consistent.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, a coding tools shopping spree. OpenAI agreed to buy Pierre Computer Company, the startup behind code review tools in Codex.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And Meta?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Meta bought Conductor. Its software lets developers run several AI coding agents at once, each in a separate workspace. The Neuron reports its hosted service shuts down on November 20.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it is one head chef running several kitchens at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Nice. OpenAI also plans to add Pierre's Code Storage service to Codex. That is a step toward the territory of code-hosting platforms.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: What should a listener at Shopee take from that?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Engineers' coding tools could change fast, as big players chase the whole workbench. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One line: the big names are buying their way into AI coding.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today. Before you automate a task, run a break-even check. The Neuron suggests it.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Break-even, like a shop deciding whether a new machine pays for itself?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Yes. First, time one manual run. Then estimate the setup time, and the review time for each run. That tells you how many repeats it takes to pay back.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And if the sums are unclear?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: There is a prompt that asks a chatbot to recommend automating, assisting or keeping the task manual. Paste in your numbers and see what it says.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Good reality check: Uber saw only four agent-booked rides in Halloween week. Not everything needs automating.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Rapid fire. Moonshot AI published the downloadable weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro, which reads text and images.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: The weights total about 1.56 terabytes, so running it locally needs serious hardware.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Pangram Image 1.0 detects AI images and video, and shows on a heatmap where the AI appears.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Oracle scrapped a $7B deal to lease Tencent AI chips after US objections.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: And Apple reportedly cut some engineers' daily AI limits to save cost.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Grok Bot now makes phone calls for paid users, who stay legally responsible for each call.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, back to where we started. US voters backed limits on data centers in nearly every local vote counted so far.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: AI needs buildings, and the neighbours get a vote.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The full digest with links is in the newsletter.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Thanks for listening, and enjoy your kopi, lah.

title: Siri opens up, Google's school switch, ChatGPT's reach
points: Apple opened Siri AI to all developers in betas; customers wait until App Store submissions start in spring.
Google will switch Search and Gemini off by default for school student accounts, tying Search to AI settings.
OpenAI says ChatGPT handles about a fifth of Google's search queries and has 1.2 billion weekly users.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Apple has opened Siri AI to every app developer, so your everyday apps could soon plug straight into your phone's assistant.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So Siri might finally do more than set my timer.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily, Thursday 5 November 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things in thirty seconds. One: Apple opened Siri AI to all developers in betas. Customers wait until App Store submissions start in spring.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Two: Google will switch Search and Gemini off by default for school student accounts, tying Search to AI settings.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three: OpenAI says ChatGPT handles about a fifth of Google's search queries, and has 1.2 billion weekly users.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: First, Apple. Its latest betas include a developer preview of Siri AI. Any app can add its own actions, and multi-step skills, to the assistant.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So can I use it tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: No. Developers can only test internally for now. App Store submissions start in spring. It is also unavailable in the EU and for under-13s.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Think of a food court with one stall called Siri. Now every app can open its own stall, and Siri takes your order for all of them.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, it could be worth watching whether shoppers one day ask their phone to do things inside an app, without opening it. Developers get to build first. Customers get the result later.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So the one thing to remember: customers wait until spring.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Next, Google. Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default for school student accounts until administrators enable them.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Search too? Why would Search switch off?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Google's education vice president said Search and AI are deeply integrated, so AI-free schools would lose Search.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Critics pushed back, right?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Yes, including Lina Khan. Google says schools stay in control.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: It is like a combo meal. If you refuse the drink, the fries go too.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For teams building products, it could be worth watching how AI gets tied to basic tools, and who holds the off switch. The question for any company is whether turning off one feature quietly switches off another.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember this: for those schools, no AI could mean no Search.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, OpenAI. A product lead said ChatGPT handles roughly one fifth as many queries as Google.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: That is a serious dent. What about users?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Weekly users rose from 1 billion to 1.2 billion in about two months. Voice mode alone has 250 million weekly users.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: That is like a new stall near the MRT that already draws a fifth of the biggest stall's crowd.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: He also said most people do not seem to mind ads. For marketing teams, it could be worth watching whether shoppers start searches in a chatbot. For Shopee, that could mean customers discover products through a chatbot first.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So the number to remember is 1.2 billion weekly users. Quite a crowd, lah.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Now, try this. A Rundown guide shows how to build a small Runway app that turns one product photo into three studio shots: coral, sunlit and blue-lit.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So a seller snaps one photo and gets three looks. Any catch?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Start from the original photo each time. That way flaws do not carry over from one shot to the next.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So today, pick one product, make all three shots, and put them side by side. See which one you would click on.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Then try a second product the same way, and note which look you prefer.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Rapid fire time. GitHub says agents started 40% of pull requests in September, up from 17% six months earlier. Pull requests are proposed code changes.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: CrowdStrike launched an AI Kill Switch that cuts a rogue agent's link to its model. A human admin must trigger it, and each use is logged.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Menlo Ventures says enterprise AI spending rose fivefold in a year, to $177 billion. It measures spending, not returns.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And OpenAI now offers up to $172,000 per critical security find.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, back to where we began: Siri AI is open to developers, but customers wait until spring.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Open doors today, real customers in spring.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The full digest with links is in the newsletter.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: That was AI Kopi Daily. Catch you tomorrow, and finish your kopi.

title: Anthropic's $895B bill, and AI editing AI
points: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows about $895B in spending commitments, alongside fast revenue growth and large losses.
MIT researchers had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra edit a small model's weights, lifting its math score from 7.9% to 48.1%.
Musk said Grok Bot cost too much to serve, and OpenAI launched a plan to cut data center power use at peak times.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Anthropic's amended IPO filing lists about $895 billion in spending commitments.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Sorry, billion with a B? That's one very big kopi bill lah.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Yes, and it sits beside fast revenue growth and large losses.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily, for Wednesday 4 November 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things today. One: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows about $895 billion in commitments, alongside fast revenue growth and large losses.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Two: MIT researchers had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra edit a small model's weights, lifting its math score from 7.9% to 48.1%.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three: Musk said Grok Bot cost too much to serve, and OpenAI launched a plan to cut data center power use at peak times.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Story one. Anthropic's updated IPO filing lists about $895 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments. Roughly $448 billion of that is due by the end of 2030.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And what's coming in?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third-quarter revenue was about $17 billion, with a $23.3 billion net loss. TLDR AI puts the net loss for the first nine months at $104 billion.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it's like signing a lease on a huge hawker centre before the crowds arrive. Revenue is growing fast, but the losses are big too.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The filing also says upcoming models could imminently cross its safety line for AI-driven progress.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Imminently. That's a strong word. So what does it mean for us?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, it could be worth watching how this shapes the price of AI tools. That is a thought, not a fact.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One thing to remember: huge commitments, huge losses, fast growth.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Story two. MIT researchers had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra rewrite 0.016% of a small Qwen model's weights. Those are the numbers that govern its behaviour.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And did it work?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Its math score rose from 7.9% to 48.1%, without retraining. But it did little for Gemma 3, and the work is not yet peer reviewed.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it's like a tutor who doesn't make you redo the school year, just fixes a few key habits. Then the grades jump.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For teams at a company like Shopee, it could point to cheaper ways to improve small models. Worth watching, but it is early.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember this: a tiny edit, a big jump, but one model so far, and not yet peer reviewed.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Story three. Users hit weekly usage caps on Grok Bot. Elon Musk said its serving cost was unsustainably high relative to revenue.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So is anyone paying?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: AI Secret reports 800,000 paying weekly users, with plans up to $200 a month.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And the cost?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Superhuman AI notes Musk gave no specifics.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Like a buffet where everyone keeps going back for seconds. Sooner or later, the owner limits the plates.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For people at a company like Shopee, it could be worth watching whether AI tools bring tighter limits or higher prices.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: The takeaway: serving AI costs real money, and caps may follow.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today. Superhuman AI has a tutorial for building a daily brand pulse from X with Grok Bot.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Okay, what do I actually do?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Create a Bot that tracks your brand, products and competitors on X. Test it once, then prune the noisy keywords.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Then save it as a Skill and schedule a morning summary of mentions, trends, risks and opportunities.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Run it once first and prune before you schedule anything, so the summary isn't full of noise. Marketing teams could try it today with their own brand and competitor names.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Test once, prune, then schedule. Basically a morning briefing that writes itself.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Quick ones now, one sentence each.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Anthropic added message threads to its Claude API, the connection apps use to reach Claude, so apps send only new messages, and median time to first token is about 35% lower for requests of 500K to 1M tokens.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: OpenAI plans to merge the Chat and Work tabs in ChatGPT, after testing with select users.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Proton's CEO dropped plans to re-interview nearly all staff about their AI use after pushback, as staff feared low AI use could cost jobs, according to 404 Media.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Marvell will buy Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal, described as one of tech's largest takeovers.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, back to that $895 billion. Huge commitments, huge losses, fast growth. That is the one line to take with you.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Billion with a B, I'll remember. And the full digest, with links, is in the newsletter.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily. Thanks for listening, and see you tomorrow.

title: Haiku from Orbit, Votes on Earth
points: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite ran its first AI prompt in orbit, returning a haiku; costs and orbital crowding remain open questions.
Data centers are on ballots in about 20 US communities this week, as OpenAI reportedly plans to rebrand them.
Anthropic renamed its Max plans, removed the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra users, and will watermark text from its models.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Google just got an AI to write a haiku from space. A real satellite, in orbit.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So the poetry is officially out of this world. Who's paying for the rocket?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: We'll get there. This is AI Kopi Daily, Tuesday, 3 November 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things in thirty seconds. One: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite ran its first AI prompt in orbit and returned a haiku. Costs and orbital crowding remain open questions.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Two: data centers are on ballots in about 20 US communities this week, as OpenAI reportedly plans to rebrand them.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three: Anthropic renamed its Max plans, removed the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra users, and will watermark text from its models.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Let's start in orbit. Google's Project Suncatcher prototype ran the Gemma 4 model on a data-center-class chip in space, then sent a haiku back via Svalbard.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Impressive. But how much computer is actually up there?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Four chips, but the craft can run only one, in roughly 20-minute bursts. If the chips pass radiation and heat tests, two more satellites will launch in 2027 to test laser links.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it's a hawker stall with four stoves, and only one allowed on, 20 minutes at a time.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: That's the idea, lah. And Google's energy chief says space data centers can cost up to 100 times more than Earth ones. Experts also worry about crowded orbits, debris and conflict.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, this could be a faraway signal about where computing power comes from, and what it costs. Worth watching, not budgeting for. The one thing: it worked, but the cost question is still open.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Back on Earth. Roughly 20 US communities are voting on data center bans or pauses in this week's midterms.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So voters get a say on the big building next door.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Yes. OpenAI reportedly plans to rebrand the sites as "AI compute campuses" and pitch them as local job creators. Some Democrats want a federal freeze on new data centers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Same building, new signboard. Like renaming a factory a production campus.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Could be. For a company like Shopee, it could mean computing power gets tangled in local politics, which might one day touch the cost of the AI tools teams use. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: The one thing: where AI lives is now a question on a ballot.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Now a plan change at Anthropic. Max 5x is now just Max, at $100 a month. Max 20x becomes Ultra, at $200 a month. Same prices.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So what actually changes?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Verified Ultra accounts no longer face the 5-hour usage limit. Weekly limits stay. Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until verified.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Like tapping through the MRT gantry. Once you're checked, you walk straight in, but the weekly limit still applies.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Anthropic also says it will watermark text from its models, to comply with EU rules. SpaceX says Grok API text will be watermarked from November 7.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: For teams at Shopee using these tools, it could mean checking which plan heavy users are on. Worth a look. The one thing: same price, fewer interruptions for verified Ultra.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today. Claude has a feature called Artifacts that can build a small internal tool.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: For people who don't code?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: It's a step-by-step guide. Pick a repetitive task. Upload a real example. Then prompt for upload, process and export features.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Then test it with real inputs, and share it with coworkers. So the chore you hate could become one button.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Start small. One task, one real example, then see how it goes.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Rapid fire. AI Secret reports OpenAI sought $30 billion at over $1.4 trillion, but had about $11 billion committed by the deadline.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: It cut the target to $20 billion at $1.25 trillion, and is turning to family offices and wealthy individuals.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: DoorDash has received only "several hundred" orders from AI agents, against 3 million daily deliveries.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Apple will bring Apple Intelligence to iPhones in China using Alibaba's Qwen, with a public release in December.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: And Reddit's CEO says AI Mode no longer sends traffic. Search referrals fell over 1 million a week, and the site will require sign-in.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, from a haiku in orbit to votes on the ground, AI's physical footprint was today's story.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One line to remember: AI wrote a poem in space, but the bill and the neighbours are still unsettled.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The full digest with links is in the newsletter. Thanks for listening.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Have a good day, everyone.

title: Mistral Opens Large 4, Claude Reviews Itself
points: Mistral released downloadable weights for its trillion-parameter Large 4 model, targeting self-hosted enterprise and cybersecurity use.
NYT reports US intelligence found an alleged Chinese asset built close ties with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; nothing proven yet.
Anthropic says Claude has been quietly reviewing its own chats since June to flag misuse, catching large-scale abuse cases.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: A trillion-parameter model, and Mistral just released the weights so companies can run it on their own servers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Hold on. A model that big, on a company's own machines? That is a big deal lah.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily, Monday 2 November 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things today. First, Mistral released downloadable weights for its trillion-parameter Large 4 model, aimed at self-hosted enterprise and cybersecurity use.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Second, the New York Times reports US intelligence found an alleged Chinese asset who built close ties with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Nothing is proven yet.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, Anthropic says its assistant Claude has been quietly reviewing its own chats since June, to flag misuse.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Story one. Mistral released open weights for Large 4, a trillion-parameter model it calls Le Chonk. Weights are the trained model itself. Instead of calling a cloud API, which means renting access over the internet, a company can run it on its own servers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: A trillion sounds heavy. Does every question wake up the whole thing?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: It activates only about 49 billion parameters per query. That is the number to hold onto. Mistral claims leading open-weight results on coding and cybersecurity benchmarks. A stronger cyber-focused variant stays restricted to vetted partners.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Think of it like owning the recipe instead of ordering delivery. You cook in your own kitchen, on your own stove.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, it could mean more choice about where sensitive data is processed. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One thing to remember: open weights means you can run it yourself. Large 4 is the one to watch, nickname Le Chonk and all.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Story two. The New York Times reports US intelligence found a Singapore-based data-center executive who built close ties with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The executive was allegedly passing information to Beijing.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Heavy claim. And this one lands close to home, since the executive is Singapore-based. What is actually established?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Very little so far. The report says Trump was briefed about a year ago. Nvidia calls the meetings routine business. Nothing about what, if anything, was shared has been proven.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it is like a rumour at the hawker centre. Interesting, but you wait for the facts before you pick a side.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, it could be a reminder that AI hardware partnerships may draw close attention. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember this: it is an allegation, not a finding. Nothing about what was shared is proven, so hold your judgment.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Story three. Anthropic says Claude has been quietly reviewing its own conversations since June. It rates each one for potential harm, so cases can be prioritized for human review.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Has it worked?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: It helped surface over 100,000 child-abuse flags from one API customer, plus a romance-scam operation. But in red-team tests, where testers play the attacker, it only modestly reduced successful attacks.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it is like a security guard watching the CCTV. He spots trouble and calls a person, but he does not stop every break-in.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: That is why humans stay in the loop. The system helps rank cases so reviewers know where to look first.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Over 100,000 flags from one customer. For an online marketplace, that could hint at how scam and abuse spotting might work at scale. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The takeaway: the AI sorts the cases, humans make the call.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today. The Rundown has a guide on ElevenLabs Audio Tags, which help Eleven v4 voiceovers sound more natural.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: I am not an audio person. Where do I start?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Save a plain version of your script first. Then make a tagged version and compare the two. Change just one cue at a time.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Like seasoning soup. One pinch, then taste. You can even test a two-speaker dialogue, as the guide does.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: A short script for a product update could be a good first test. Compare, then keep whichever sounds better.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Amazon's AWS posted its fastest sales growth in nearly five years, up 39 percent to $46 billion, but free cash flow flipped from a $14.8 billion inflow to a $42.4 billion outflow.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Meta's Style Sketch builds virtual wardrobes and outfit try-ons from Instagram photos, launching first in Singapore, Indonesia and Thailand.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: OpenAI now gives Pro and Business ChatGPT subscribers up to $500 a month in free API credits.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Cohere announced a Series E targeting up to $5 billion, citing 165 percent year-over-year revenue growth.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So the one-liner: Mistral just put a trillion-parameter model into companies' own hands.

transcript.speaker: Raj

title: Claude Duet, PHP Flaws and OpenAI on Google
points: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that works autonomously while you're away, in preview for US Pro/Max users.
AI models (GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini) found two critical PHP flaws letting hackers hijack servers without login; patches are now live.
OpenAI's models and Codex agent tool are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden, plus Google's Antigravity and Gemini Agent soon.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Anthropic just launched Claude Duet, an AI agent that keeps working on its own cloud computer even when your devices are off.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it works the night shift while I sleep. Can it do my kopi run too?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Approval first, Raj. This is AI Kopi Daily, Friday 23 October 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things in thirty seconds. One: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive agent that works autonomously while you're away. It's in preview for US Pro and Max users.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Two: AI models, including GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini, found two critical PHP flaws that let hackers hijack servers without a login. Patches are now live.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three: OpenAI's models and its Codex agent tool are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden. Google's Antigravity and Gemini Agent follow soon.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: First, Claude Duet. It is built on Opus 5.5. It monitors your connected apps, sends morning briefs, and works on its own cloud computer. Most of the big newsletters covered it.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Why does the cloud computer matter?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The work carries on even when your phone and laptop are off.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Hold on. Does it just go and spend my money?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: No. It asks for approval before payments, messages or deletions. For now it is a research preview for waitlisted US Pro and Max subscribers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it's like a new colleague who tidies your desk before you arrive, but still asks you to sign off on anything that matters.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Exactly. For a company like Shopee, it could mean routine morning checks get prepared before the team logs in. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One thing to remember: the agent works while you're away, and approval is the safety catch.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Next, security. Researchers using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, and separately Wiz using Gemini, found two critical flaws in PHP. Both efforts used AI models to find them.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: PHP. Is that some niche thing?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Not at all. It is used by roughly 70% of websites. The flaws let attackers hijack servers without logging in.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Roughly 70 percent is a big slice of the web. So it's a door that opens for anyone who walks up and pushes. Is there a fix yet?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Yes. Patches shipped after about two months of coordination. The NSA urged immediate patching or taking systems offline, and some government sites went dark.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: For teams like ours, it could be a prompt to ask whether anything we run on PHP is patched. One thing to remember: AI is now helping find serious security holes.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, OpenAI's frontier models and its Codex coding agent will be offered through Google Cloud's Model Garden.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Rivals on one shelf? Like two hawker stalls sharing a food court?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Pretty much. Each keeps its own cooking, but customers walk in through one door. They come paired with Google's access controls and infrastructure for enterprise customers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And where else will they show up?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Inside Google's Antigravity coding tool and the Gemini Agent, soon.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So what could that mean for a company like Shopee?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Teams already on Google Cloud might get OpenAI models alongside Google's own, under the same access controls. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One thing to remember: choosing a model and choosing a cloud may become two separate decisions.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today: have an AI assistant draft your meeting brief.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Walk me through it. I'm not an engineer.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: You connect a personal AI assistant to your email and calendar. It catches schedule changes, checks open tasks, and prepares a short meeting brief.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And it won't go rogue and email my boss?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: You can save the steps as a reusable routine that only runs with your approval. Start with low-risk, read-first tasks before letting it send anything.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Small start, same safety catch.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Meta plans to give every shareholder one non-voting share for each share they hold, to fund AI spending without diluting Mark Zuckerberg's control.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Recursive released Flint, an open-source model for AI coding on a laptop, keeping code off remote servers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: OpenAI expanded ChatGPT ads to 26 more countries, bringing the total to 89, shown only to Free and Go plan users.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: And a tampered LiteLLM package was live for about two hours before removal, stealing user credentials.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, back to where we started: Claude Duet, and agents that keep working while you're away.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Let them work, but keep your thumb on the approve button, lah.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The full digest with links is in the newsletter. Thanks for listening, and see you next time on AI Kopi Daily.

title: DeepSeek's free engine, scorpion proteins, OpenAI buys
points: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the engine behind its production AI service, free for anyone to deploy.
Anthropic's Claude autonomously designed 318,000 scorpion-antivenom candidate proteins; 17 bound their target in lab tests.
OpenAI acquired drug-trial startup Orchestra Bio, while Altman told staff AI's endgame may need a global regulator.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: DeepSeek just gave away the engine that runs its own AI service, for free.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Free? That's like a famous hawker handing out the recipe and the stove.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily, for Thursday, 22 October 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things today. First, DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the engine behind its production AI service, free for anyone to deploy.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Second, Anthropic's Claude autonomously designed 318,000 scorpion-antivenom candidate proteins. 17 bound their target in lab tests.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, OpenAI acquired drug-trial startup Orchestra Bio, while Altman told staff AI's endgame may need a global regulator.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Let's start with DeepSeek. It released DeepInfer, the software that runs its DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model in production. Anyone can use it commercially, for free.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: In plain terms, what is an inference engine?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: It's the part that answers your questions once a model is trained. The company says it processes huge volumes of tokens daily on Nvidia and Huawei chips.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So training is learning to cook. Inference is the kitchen serving thousands of plates at lunch rush.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Exactly. Several newsletters reported it as a way to cut the cost of running large AI models at scale. And this is the same software behind DeepSeek's live service.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, that could mean cheaper AI features, say in search or customer chat. Worth watching. Remember: the kitchen blueprint is now free.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Next, scorpion antivenom. Investment firm Citrini Research used Anthropic's Claude, almost entirely unsupervised, to design over 318,000 candidate proteins meant to block scorpion venom toxins.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: That's a lot of candidates. Did any work?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: They sent 211 for lab testing. Outside labs confirmed 17 bind their target toxin. But none have been shown to actually neutralize venom or protect against stings.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it's 17 keys that fit the lock, but nobody has opened the door yet.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Good picture. And note that Citrini is an investment firm, not a drug lab.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: For teams at a company like Shopee, it could be a pattern worth watching: let AI draft huge numbers of options, then people check the few that matter. Remember: 17 bound their target, none proven to neutralize venom.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, OpenAI bought Orchestra Bio, a startup whose AI agents track how a delay in one part of a drug study affects the rest of the program.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So like one stalled MRT train slowing the whole line, and the agents spot the knock-on effects?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: That's the idea. The deal folds Orchestra Bio into Rosalind, OpenAI's existing suite of life-sciences AI tools.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Meanwhile, Altman reportedly told staff the industry could end in a global watchdog, a single merged super-lab, or one company racing ahead of every rival.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: He called the last option terrible, and said OpenAI must pick a path within a year.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Tracking knock-on delays could be worth watching in any complex operation, even at a company like Shopee. Remember: OpenAI just bought a drug-trial coordinator.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Now, try this today. Anthropic shared a method for using Claude to understand a spreadsheet you inherited, before touching it.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Because we've all opened a file full of mystery formulas.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Step one, ask Claude to decode the formulas, the color-coding and the hidden assumptions. Step two, have it list risks in an issue log. No edits yet.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And after that?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Only after you review, ask it to add new data, keeping existing formulas intact.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So read first, then write. Simple enough to try before lunch.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Quick round. Bob McGrew, OpenAI's former chief research officer, launched factory-AI startup Arda, which raised $160M at a $1.5B valuation.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: ChatGPT now lets you lock sensitive chats behind a PIN or Face ID.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Meta paused Muse's chat-sharing after researchers found thousands of shared chats, some confidential, via public internet records.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: And SpaceX's renamed Super Intelligence AI unit made $7.56B in revenue this quarter, mostly from renting data-center capacity to rival AI labs.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Back to where we started: DeepSeek gave away its engine, reportedly a way to cut the cost of running big AI models.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One thing to take with your kopi: the kitchen blueprint is now free. The full digest with links is in the newsletter.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Thanks for listening, see you tomorrow lah.

title: Cheap AI, Fast Models, and a $50 Break-In
points: Inception's Mercury 3 diffusion model claims speed and quality edge over GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.
MiniMax's M3.1 Flash cuts agent costs 70% and triples inference speed versus its predecessor.
US DHS ordered agencies to purge DeepSeek, while hackers used AI agents to breach 100+ companies.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Hackers used AI agents to break into more than 100 company websites, and it reportedly cost about $50 a break-in.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Fifty dollars per break-in. That is a very cheap day at work for a hacker.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: This is AI Kopi Daily, Wednesday 21 October 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things today. First, Inception's Mercury 3 diffusion model claims a speed and quality edge over GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Second, MiniMax says its M3.1 Flash cuts agent costs 70 percent and triples inference speed versus its predecessor.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, the US Department of Homeland Security ordered agencies to purge DeepSeek, while hackers used AI agents to breach more than 100 companies.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Let's start with the hackers. Security firm NorForge found unsecured control panels for an AI hacking tool called Cairn. They showed one hacker using AI agents to break into over 100 company websites.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Anyone big?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins were among them. NorForge estimates each successful break-in cost roughly $50 in AI fees, using tools like Claude Code and DeepSeek's cheap model.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it is like a burglar who once needed years of training, and now rents a cheap robot that tries every door.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: For a company like Shopee, it could mean more attempts against websites, at lower cost to attackers. How security teams respond is worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Cheaper for attackers, then. The one thing to remember: about $50 a break-in.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Next, speed. Inception launched Mercury 3, a diffusion-based large language model. Instead of writing one word at a time, it drafts and refines many words at once.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Like a kitchen plating ten bowls of noodles together, instead of one bowl at a time.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: That is the idea. Inception says it is 4-8x faster than rivals and can generate over 1,000 tokens per second. It also says quality matches or beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Tokens being the small chunks of text the model writes out. And the price?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: $0.20 and $0.70 per million tokens. Those are Inception's own claims, so worth checking.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: What could it mean for us?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: If the claims hold, faster replies could matter for things like customer chat. That is only a thought for now.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember: 4-8x faster, says Inception.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Third, MiniMax launched M3.1 Flash. It is the production version of a previously unnamed stealth model, called Space Bunny.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Space Bunny. What does it do?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: MiniMax claims big gains in coding, computer use and cybersecurity tasks. It says the model is three times faster and 70 percent cheaper to run than its predecessor.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: When can people get it?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: An open-weight release is planned for October 23.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So it is like a hawker stall that cut its prices and says it now serves three times faster.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: One analysis says cheap open models from MiniMax and DeepSeek are squeezing US pricing for budget AI. For a company like Shopee, cheaper agents could change what teams can afford to try. Worth watching.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember: 70 percent cheaper, according to MiniMax.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today. A guide shows how to use Google's Gemini 4 Argon to compare two versions of a document.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Say, an old and a new version of a policy?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Yes. Tell it which version wins when the two conflict. Then require a citation for every finding.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Any trick to get better answers?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Paste your documents before your question. Argon's large context window still has to share space between your input and its reasoning.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So documents first, question last. Try it on a document you already know, so you can check the citations.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Quick hits. Anthropic's free OSS Scanner reported 77 critical and 803 high-severity findings in open-source projects in its first week.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: A Google DeepMind study found that wrong user hints cut AI agent success by almost 50 percent.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: The Department of Homeland Security gave federal civilian agencies 60 days to request exceptions to its DeepSeek order.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: And Anthropic and Nscale are reportedly negotiating a second $45 billion compute deal, barely a month after the first.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, back to where we started. AI is getting cheaper and faster, and that includes for attackers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: About $50 a break-in. Worth remembering over your kopi.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The full digest with links is in the newsletter. This was AI Kopi Daily. See you tomorrow.

title: Anthropic's $48B pledge, DeepSeek's price cut
points: Anthropic commits 5% equity (about $48B) to a new Public Benefit Fund for workers hit by AI.
DeepSeek's cheaper open-weight model and new web-search APIs undercut US rivals on price and speed.
OpenAI's mystery 'Aurora' image models and a new Chrome computer-use feature surfaced over the weekend.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Anthropic says it will put 5 percent of its equity, about $48 billion, into a fund for workers hit by AI.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: That is serious kopi money. Who gets it?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: We'll get there. This is AI Kopi Daily, Tuesday 20 October 2026.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three things today. One: Anthropic commits 5 percent of its equity, about $48 billion, to a new Public Benefit Fund for workers hit by AI.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Two: DeepSeek's cheaper open-weight model and new web-search services undercut US rivals on price and speed.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Three: OpenAI's mystery Aurora image models and a new Chrome computer-use feature surfaced over the weekend.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Back to Anthropic. It plans to give an initial 5 percent of its equity to a new Public Benefit Fund. That is about $48 billion at its last valuation. It still needs shareholder approval, and more would be added as the company's value grows.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So who can actually get the money?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The fund can donate to nonprofits or pay specific groups directly, including workers hit by AI. It cannot fund political causes.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Like a hawker setting aside a slice of every day's takings for neighbours who lose their stalls.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Nice picture. For a company like Shopee, it could signal that support for displaced workers is becoming part of the AI conversation. Worth watching whether others follow.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One thing to remember: 5 percent, pending shareholder approval.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Mei: DeepSeek released an open-weight model called V4.1-Flash-1017. Open-weight means the model's inner settings are published for others to run. DeepSeek says it beats Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 on its own coding benchmark, while running faster and far cheaper.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Its own benchmark. That's a stall owner grading his own chicken rice.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Fair, so treat the claim carefully. DeepSeek also opened pay-per-call Search and Fetch services for web browsing, priced well below rivals. They are free until November 1 for agents built on Claude Code or Codex.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And agents are AI helpers that carry out tasks, right?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Right. For teams at a company like Shopee, cheaper models and search could change what it costs to test an AI idea. Worth watching, not a conclusion.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Remember this: cheaper, and free until November 1 for some agents.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Anthropic's own workforce study found junior staff fell from 27 percent to 9 percent of technical hires since early 2025.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So AI is doing their work?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: The data points that way. By August, AI agents run by employees logged six times the hours of the humans operating them. Engineers ship far more code, but reviewing and supervising agents has become the real bottleneck.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Like a kitchen with many fast cooks and one chef who has to taste every dish.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Exactly. At a company like Shopee, it could mean checking work matters more than producing it. Worth watching how entry-level roles change.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: The takeaway: the bottleneck moves from making to checking.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Try this today. Claude Code can turn a folder of notes, screenshots or reports into a slide deck. Point it at the folder and ask for a polished deck. It arrives as an editable Slides artifact.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And if slide three is rubbish?

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Refine individual slides by chatting with it. Then export to PowerPoint, PDF or Google Slides.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So messy notes become a presentable deck before your kopi gets cold.

transcript.text: Quick ones. A Wharton survey of over 1,400 US enterprise leaders found only 7 percent of companies succeed at proving AI's value, reshaping workflows and aligning the organisation.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Disney agreed to hire over 60 Character.AI employees for about $60 million a year in pay, in a bankruptcy-sale bid a rival could still beat.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN each fell over 20 percent last week, which Goldman Sachs links to rising borrowing costs for data-center buildouts.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And China proposed export controls on 23 AI-related items, though access through apps and software connections would stay open.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: So, back to where we started: Anthropic is pledging 5 percent of its equity, about $48 billion, toward workers hit by AI.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: A big pledge, still pending approval. The full digest with links is in the newsletter.

transcript.speaker: Mei
transcript.text: That's AI Kopi Daily. See you tomorrow.
